text.p: Harley-Davidson Inc said Thursday it raised its 1997 production goal to 130,000 units from the previously announced 127,000.
The company shipped 118,771 motorcycles in 1996, the company said.
Earlier Thursday, the company reported fourth quarter operating net income of $37.3 million, or $0.49 a share, compared to $30.1 million, or $0.40 a share a year ago.

The improved fourth quarter results are attributable primarily to an increase in motorcycle unit shipments and improved manufacturing efficiencies, the company said. Fourth quarter unit shipments totaled 29,835 units, up 1,561 units from a year ago.
But fourth quarter Genuine Motor Parts and Genuine Motor Accessories sales were $41.8 million, a $5.0 million decrease from the year-ago quarter, the company said.

"The fourth quarter was adversely impacted by a variety of factors, including: our failure to bring to market some new product introductions on schedule, four fewer shipping days, and the transition to our new P&A distribution center," Harley-Davison chief executive Rich Teerlink said in a news release.
